NO. 043 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Recurvirostridae · Stilts & Avocets

Black-winged Stilt

黑翅长脚鹬 · hēi chì cháng jiǎo yù Himantopus himantopus
Winter visitor / passage Common 33–40 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A bird on a pair of pink stilts

A body in sharp black and white, on legs of an absurd pink length — the Black-winged Stilt walks like a model on stilts. It is the most elegant figure on the mudflat, and one of the easiest waders to identify.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • LegsExtremely long, pink to red, about half the bird's height — the origin of the name.
  • ColourUpperparts black (with a metallic gloss on the male's back), underparts white; the extent of black on the nape and crown varies with individual and sex.
  • BillBlack, fine and straight as a needle, made for picking small invertebrates out of shallow water.
  • FlightIn flight the legs trail far behind like two ribbons; the underwing is boldly black and white.

Behaviour

Often wades slowly in shallow water, pecking rapidly at the surface or the mud as it goes. Sociable, gathering in winter in parties of dozens and mixing with Kentish Plovers and greenshanks. It defends the nest vigorously, luring predators away with a broken-wing display. In South China mostly a winter visitor and passage migrant.

Voice

Field recording

Recording Joost van Bruggen · Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 · Original file

A loud, sharp 'kik—kik—kik' or 'kee-ack', often repeated on take-off or when alarmed — one of the most audible sounds on a mudflat.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qi'ao Island tidal flats
  • Jinwan salt pans
  • Hengqin wetlands
  • Doumen shallow ponds
Field note
From a distance it looks like a row of black and white dots on pink sticks — once you see the legs there is little doubt. In winter flocks, check for smaller, shorter-legged species mixed in.
